data.narrative:
Reverion is a Series B climate and energy company that has raised $79M to date. The valuation analysis triangulates across a peer set of 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies (KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy), supplemented by a broader comp universe of 8 private peers and 1 public comparable (Lanzatech, ticker LNZA).

Two methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $79M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage step-ups, implying a valuation of $150M. Peer-median analysis benchmarks Reverion against the three Climate & Energy peers noted above; the median valuation across this cohort is $1.0B, with a range of $700M to $3.0B. These peers trade at substantially higher valuations despite comparable or more advanced stages, reflecting sector maturity and investor appetite for decarbonization technologies.

The two methods produce a wide spread. The triangulated range spans $128M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median implied valuation of $575M. This disparity reflects structural tension between capital-efficiency metrics (stage-progression) and peer trading multiples in a growth-stage, high-conviction sector. Key uncertainties include Reverion's unit economics relative to peers, revenue trajectory, and whether recent market repricing of climate-tech valuations has fundamentally shifted comparable multiples. A Series B valuation within the $400M–$700M range would reconcile both methods, though data gaps on Reverion's revenue and growth rate limit precision.
